answer: An attacker who floods the jury with fake votes also floods itself with the cost of its own dishonest votes, because every vote is penalized when it backs a bad answer. Consequently, an attacker with a large flock pays more to keep it alive than it can ever extract, which is why Sybil campaigns fail here.. The design works because cost compounds over compute, time, and reputation, growing faster than the influence the cluster can extract. Consider a umber as the anchor of the cost.
